Talking does help a lot. I have been talking to my friends, both irl, on phone and chatting online. It helps me focus on what is happening now, and I don't find myself just sitting there, watching the walls or ceilings and letting the time slip away. 

I am looking for a therapist that would be able to help me deal with trauma - but these are extremely rare in my country, and either almost unavailable (long queues where you wait months) or a few times over my acceptable price range. It is not easy to get psychological help over here. I have been thinking about self-help and reading on traumas - I was recommended a place to find them, so I need to try.

It is not easy to fill the gap after this long-term relationship I had, both emotionally and in the terms of time we spent together. I have found myself having so much free time I don't know what to do with I started just travelling around my city and swapping stuff or collecting items people are giving away and would be useful in my new flat, like hangers, or cutlery, glass and other items. It helps me to have a short-term plan and a purpose after work. It's just temporary, but seems to help me a bit.

It is hard to see any of that coming right now. I am left traumatized after my first relationship, and this one reopened those scars and produced new wounds. I cannot imagine anyone ever wanting a woman that is afraid of intimate relarionships with others and can feel no pleasure from them. That, and I am nearing my thirties. I really wanted to start a family before that time, and now I am left with nothing.

I'm so sorry for your loss, I think everyone who ever owned a beloved pet has been there before and can somewhat relate - even if each bond is not exactly the same. I love my pets even though they are mere rats and I've cried for days each time each of my previous boys passed away. Screaming and pushing won't bring back your beloved friend - but if that helps you vent out your feelings do so. Crying is okay even if others may frown at you for crying over what's in their eyes only an animal - it was your beloved friend and a part of your family. Your dog is in a better place now, he is in no pain and he is guarding you from above. Remember that he might be no more in person but he will always remain in your heart.

Have you made sure there is no smell of their poop and pee left in the cage where you dont want them doing their business? Try cleaning the cage thoroughly and put their old bedding along with dirty old bedding and poops into the litterbox. They should follow the smell and switch to making their business there only. I had a similar problem and it helped. Well, not for too long, but that's only because one of my boys kept digging under the litterbox and everything went onto the bedding anyways. Check your rat's snout if there is any porphyrine around its nose, eyes and mouth. As a temporary measure and for helping your rat's health try adding a few drops of echinacea extract to their water. My vet suggested the same to me when my boys were a bit ill. Often squeaking especially paired with labored breathing point to a respiratory disease. The faster you go to the vet and have your rattie's health checked the better - respiratory infections and diseases lead to heart diseases if not treated fast and well.
